features: NO DATABASE CHANGES — A security beta: the three flaws reported by kta1kri (PR #48), the four queue items found in the same review (183–186), and what three rounds of adversarial review found around them. Two flaws could be reached without any permission granted by hand, and one without even logging in: anyone using the residents' portal should update. Changes of behaviour are listed first.

CHANGED: MAIL, CRON AND THE EMAIL LOG — They open only with the «Manage general settings» permission, which by default only the administrator has. From 1.9.0 to 1.11.0-beta.38 being logged in was enough: residents, suppliers and collaborators opened the three pages by typing the address.

CHANGED: THE LIST OF BUILDINGS — /fetch-condomini answers only to those who manage: administrator, collaborator, anyone with «Admin panel access» or «View buildings». Residents and suppliers get 403. The /condomini/options route, which no page used, is gone too.

CHANGED: DOCUMENTS DOWNLOADED FROM THE PORTAL — A resident can download by id only the documents shown in their own list: published and approved, or uploaded by them. A document addressed to one resident stays theirs; a building document belongs to the whole building. Documents uploaded from a unit's page (deeds, contracts) stay with the administrator.

CHANGED: RECOVERING A RESTORE — Resume and cancel answer only while a restore is in progress, and accept at most five wrong passwords a minute. Whoever still has the restore page open is not affected by the limit.

CHANGED: CUSTOM ROLES WITHOUT THE PANEL — For roles without «Admin panel access», the edit and delete permissions on events, notices, documents and reports apply only to records of the user's own buildings. Left out: instalments and accounting tasks, unit attachments, records addressed to other people, and records that are also in someone else's building. In the list the pencil and bin icons still show on those records and lead to a 403 page: the fix is on the roadmap. Default roles do not change.

SECURITY: REPORTING A PAYMENT (reported by kta1kri) — Up to beta.38 anyone with «View events», that is every default resident and supplier, could mark as paid any event of any building, including the administrator's hidden tasks: the id was enough. Now only the person the instalment belongs to can report it, and only on an instalment.

SECURITY: REPORTS IN SOMEONE ELSE'S BUILDING (reported by kta1kri) — A resident could open a report in a building that is not theirs by giving its id. The same gap existed in events, documents and notices on the resident's side (queue 184): the building given must now be one of their own.
SECURITY: THE LIST OF BUILDINGS (reported by kta1kri) — /fetch-condomini returned the list of every building in the installation to anyone logged in.

SECURITY: MAIL AND CRON — Besides reading the recipients and subjects of every email and the cron token, any logged-in user could have the saved SMTP password sent to a server of their own through the connection test, and redirect all the installation's mail, including the administrator's password reset link.
SECURITY: UNIT DOCUMENTS — A default resident could download by id the deed or contract uploaded for someone else's unit, and the documents of their own building not yet published or approved.

SECURITY: RESTORE — After any restore, the recovery route stayed open forever, without login and without a limit on attempts: a way to try the administrator's password while bypassing the login lockout and two-factor authentication.

SECURITY: PERSONAL DATA AND PERMISSIONS GRANTED ON THEIR OWN — The page for editing a document, on the resident's side, sent the browser the list of every building and every contact, with tax code, email and phone, which the page did not read (queue 183). With an edit or delete permission granted without panel access, records of every building could be touched (queue 185): the limit described among the changes of behaviour now applies.

FOR DEVELOPERS — A new test, RotteSoloLoginTest, lists every route protected only by login and fails when a new one appears without a written reason, or when the check in the controller disappears, even just commented out. The question «is this building the user's?» has a single rule, CondominioDellUtente, and the limit on permissions granted outside the panel a single trait, PerimetroFuoriPannello.
THANKS — To kta1kri, who found and reported the first three flaws. Their two commits go in under their name.
